target_customer: African businesses importing and exporting cargo by air and sea
problem: Shipping to and from Africa is opaque and paperwork heavy, with customs clearance, documentation and trade financing handled by fragmented forwarders.
business_model: Freight forwarding and customs brokerage fees plus trade financing
product_category: Digital freight forwarder and customs broker

founders.name: Larry Oti
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on YC page; CEO per search coverage.

founders.name: Maureen Okojie
founders.background_notes: Described as co-founder in a Condia interview headline and snippet; not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Kobo360
competitors.what: Nigerian digital freight matching platform for trucking, adjacent to forwarding
competitors.traction_then: Had raised a 20M USD Series A and expanded to Kenya in 2019

competitors.name: Sendy
competitors.what: Kenyan on demand delivery platform that began offering freight services in 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly operations and customs expertise with workflow software; limited technical novelty.

defensibility.rationale: Customs relationships and operations know-how help, but forwarding is a low margin, fragmented business with many rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying found in sources opened.

market_need_then: Founder Kingsley Oti said the product was born from a lack of transparency in shipping (TechCabal feature, via search snippet); regional digital freight startups were drawing venture money by 2019 to 2020.

branding.domain_note: Uses send.ng, a Nigerian ccTLD. A separate SEND Freight (trysend.com) appears in results, relation unconfirmed.

brand_strength.rationale: Short name, but generic and shared with other firms such as Sendy and SEND Freight; no brand press found.

outcome_analysis: SEND is a small Lagos digital freight forwarder that reportedly moved over 3,000 ocean containers and expanded to Ghana and Togo, but only roughly 150K to 250K USD of funding appears in aggregators. With no large round or exit, it looks like a slow, capital light operator whose trajectory is unclear.
notes: send.ng returned HTTP 404 on fetch, so the site may be dead or moved. Funding is unverified: CB Insights and startuplist list 150K to 250K USD total with Uncovered Fund, Google for Startups Accelerator Africa and YC, no dated announcement; kept out of rounds. The 5M seed in results belongs to OnePort 365. Founding year conflicts (2017 vs 2020). No shutdown found; the Sendy shutdown in results is a different company. Education and prior employers not found. Competitors are trucking and delivery platforms rather than forwarders, noted as adjacent. The earlier statements above that no round was recorded are superseded by the completeness pass: the 150K seed of February 2021 rests on a single database (Startuplist Africa, lead Uncovered Fund). CB Insights also gives 150K total; Startup-seeker gives 250K. A SIMPET Group article says SEND raised pre-seed and seed rounds without figures. Topship's 2.5M seed is a different company.
